title: Genome-wide synthetic lethal screen unveils novel CAIX-NFS1/xCT axis as a targetable vulnerability in hypoxic solid tumors
model: SUM159PT triple-negative breast cancer cells (control vs CA9 knockout), GeCKO library A, hypoxia
contrast: CA9-KO vs control change from T0 to T11 (genotype x time interaction, 2 replicates per cell)
paper_method: Loess-normalized differential cumulative change (DCC) fitness score
paper_calls: NFS1 a top synthetic-lethal gene; iron-sulfur (ISCU, ISCA2, ABCB7, GLRX5) and redox (TXN, GSTM2/5, GSR, MOCS3) genes
barcs_calls: 10 genes at FDR 0.10 after control calibration (15 against the control null); top depleted PFN1, NDUFA6, NDUFS7, CS
named_hits: 0/10 at FDR 0.10: NFS1 #753 (p 0.046); ISCA2 #120, GLRX5 #202; others flat
verdict: BARCS does not call NFS1 or the iron-sulfur/redox set: NFS1 is lost in both genotypes and its extra loss in CA9-KO does not separate from replicate noise; BARCS's CA9-specific calls are mitochondrial metabolism genes instead.
